headline: Londonderry firefighter recovers at home after flashover injury
dek: Lt. Mike England suffered a broken leg and minor burns while searching a Rockingham Road house where crews feared people might still be inside. All residents and animals escaped safely.
body: A Londonderry firefighter is recovering at home after a flashover engulfed him during a search of a burning house, a close call that left him with a leg fracture and minor burns. Lt. Mike England was taken to a hospital after the Oct. 2 fire on Rockingham Road and had been released by the time [WMUR-TV reported](https://www.wmur.com/article/londonderry-firefighter-who-caught-fire-now-recovering-at-home/74015010) on Oct. 4. The station said England described himself as fortunate given the severity of the conditions and the limited injuries.

The incident began at about 10:07 p.m. when Londonderry’s fire communications center received a report of a structure fire at 83 Rockingham Road. Crews arrived to find smoke and flames coming from the home. Early information indicated that someone could still be inside, so firefighters entered to conduct a primary search while other crews advanced a hose line. [WHDH reported](https://whdh.com/news/watch-nh-firefighter-recovering-after-catching-fire-at-home-in-londonderry/) that England was using a thermal-imaging camera when the conditions changed without warning.

A flashover is the near-simultaneous ignition of exposed combustible materials in an enclosed space. In this case, the sudden increase in heat and fire caught England inside the building. He escaped quickly while flames engulfed his protective gear, and other firefighters put out the fire on his clothing before he was evaluated and taken to the hospital. The sequence was also described in the local [Patch account](https://patch.com/new-hampshire/nashua/amp/34945674/fiery-flashover-injures-firefighter-during-evening-house-fire-in-londonderry), which reported that the injured firefighter was treated at the scene before transport.

The search was prompted by concern that residents and pets might be trapped, but the people inside had already made it out. WMUR reported that five occupants evacuated on their own and declined medical treatment. WHDH and Patch both reported that the other occupants and animals were safely evacuated. No resident injury was reported in the accounts reviewed for this story, although the house suffered a serious fire and the cause remained under investigation.

The response expanded as the danger became clear. Patch reported that the fire grew to a second-alarm incident after the flashover, bringing additional crews from Bedford, Windham, Salem and Litchfield, along with earlier assistance from Derry and Manchester. Firefighters knocked down most of the fire and then worked through salvage and overhaul operations to deal with remaining hot spots. The mutual-aid response allowed Londonderry to add personnel while maintaining coverage for other calls in the town and neighboring communities.

England’s recovery has given the incident a different ending than the video of his escape might suggest. WMUR reported that he was home and recovering, while WHDH said Londonderry Fire Chief James Young credited England’s training and experience and expressed relief that the injuries were not more severe. The reporting does not provide a detailed medical timeline or say when England will return to duty. NorthEast News has not independently reviewed medical records or the department’s incident report.

For Londonderry, the next confirmed step is the fire investigation. Officials had not announced a cause in the reports reviewed through Oct. 6, and the available accounts do not identify a final damage estimate. The incident illustrates why an apparently routine primary search can become life-threatening in seconds: firefighters were acting on a report of possible occupants, and the interior conditions shifted before the search was complete. The town’s [Fire Department](https://www.londonderrynh.gov/366/Fire-Department) remains the local agency responsible for fire response and public updates as the investigation and England’s recovery continue.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Londonderry firefighter recovers after flashover injury
seoDescription: Lt. Mike England suffered a broken leg and minor burns during a search at a Londonderry house fire and is recovering at home.
